function.mechanism: Antimicrobial peptide activity against susceptible Gram-positive bacteria (including inhibition of Clostridium botulinum outgrowth/toxin formation in authorized uses), involving membrane-targeting bacteriocin effects.
common_food_categories: pasteurized process cheese spread with fruits/vegetables/meats
unripened cheese (EU opinion evaluated proposed extension)
heat-treated meat products (EU opinion evaluated proposed extension)

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 opinion (ON-5063): ADI derived from 90-day rat NOAEL 225 mg/kg bw/day with uncertainty factor 200; exposure estimates reported below ADI for all population groups.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern was concluded for current uses, and proposed extension to unripened cheese and heat-treated meat products was not considered of safety concern.

fda.notes: Affirmed as GRAS direct food substance under Part 184 conditions; antimicrobial use in specified pasteurized cheese spread categories, current GMP corresponding to maximum 250 ppm nisin in finished product.

adi.basis: FAO JECFA additive detail lists ADI range 0-2 mg/kg bw (full ADI).

concerns.summary: Recent animal/preclinical literature reports nisin-related microbiome composition changes; a 2026 zebrafish diabetic model reported dysbiosis, intestinal barrier disruption, and inflammatory signaling associated with worsened vascular outcomes.
In a disease-specific zebrafish model, dietary nisin was associated with exacerbation of diabetic vascular complications via NF-kB-linked inflammatory pathways.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: No adverse effects in 90-day rat study at 225 mg/kg bw/day (NOAEL) and exposure estimates below ADI for all population groups.
FDA: GRAS affirmation with specific food-category and GMP limits in 21 CFR 184.1538.
JECFA: Full ADI established (0-2 mg/kg bw) in latest listed evaluation.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2017 abstract reports overall exposure below ADI across population groups for current and proposed uses.

risk_assessment.rationale: Convergent regulatory acceptance (EFSA/FDA/JECFA) with defined ADIs and use limits supports low-to-limited risk at authorized exposures. New mechanistic animal findings suggest potential context-dependent effects (notably microbiome/inflammation in disease models), but current human evidence and regulatory actions do not support escalation to moderate or high.
key_factors: EFSA-approved with ADI 1 mg/kg bw/day and no safety concern conclusion in 2017 opinion
FDA GRAS with explicit CFR conditions and 250 ppm GMP cap in specified foods
JECFA full ADI 0-2 mg/kg bw with latest evaluation listed as 2025
Recent preclinical studies indicate possible microbiome-mediated context-specific adverse effects requiring continued monitoring
